# `⊃` — Mix / Pick

`⊃Y` assembles items into rectangular cells, padding to a common shape with fill.

```apl
⊃1 2 3             ⍝ 1 2 3
⊃[[1 2] [3 4 5]]   ⍝ [1 2 0 ⋄ 3 4 5]
```

`P⊃Y` selects leading-axis coordinates. Remaining axes form a cell; full coordinates return the stored value. Successive Picks traverse nesting. Empty coordinates return `Y`.

```apl
1⊃2 3⍴⍳6           ⍝ 3 4 5
1 1⊃2 3⍴⍳6         ⍝ 4
0⊃1⊃[[1 2] [3 4]]  ⍝ 3
⍬⊃1 2              ⍝ 1 2
```

Array-valued coordinate fields pair using leading-axis agreement:

```apl
[0 2;1 3]⊃3 4⍴⍳12  ⍝ 1 11
```

Coordinate fields may use strings on [keyed axes](../keyed.qmd).

```apl
T←["price":[1 2 3] "qty":[4 5 6]]
"qty"⊃T             ⍝ 4 5 6
["qty" "price";]⊃T ⍝ [[4 5 6] [1 2 3]]
```

With axes, `⊃⍠A Y` places the cell axes of Mix among the frame axes. See [Axis](axis.qmd). On Pick, negative positions count from the end. Position 0 or ¯1 on an empty axis gives fill, as does [First](take.qmd).

## Errors

- `RANK`: Mix axes not a scalar or vector
- `LENGTH`: Mix axis count not the cell rank
- `INDEX`: position outside the array, or Mix axis outside the result
- `DOMAIN`: repeated or fractional Mix axes
